Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara Oy. I have followed Kaikuvaara’s work in remote-sensing instrumentation for some years now, and the company’s place within Oulu’s RF and photonics engineering community is a significant part of what draws me to this role. The concentration of wireless, radar, and space-systems expertise in the region is unusual in Europe, and the prospect of working alongside the research groups, Suvanto, and the cluster of instrument companies in the area is professionally attractive in a way that few other Nordic locations can match.

I have spent the past nineteen years at Nordkom Radar Systems, where my work has covered most of the signal-processing chain from algorithm design through to delivered flight hardware. The project I am most proud of is the digital beamforming pipeline I designed for a 64-element L-band phased-array receiver built for a maritime surveillance radar. I was responsible for the entire receive path: spatial sampling, per-element gain and phase correction, subarray summation, and adaptive null steering. The array’s wide scan-angle requirement demanded careful grating-lobe suppression and mutual-coupling compensation across the full steering range. Taking that design from a MATLAB proof-of-concept through to a working receiver that met its sidelobe specification against measured sea-clutter data was the most complete piece of systems engineering I have done.

A large part of the same programme required embedded real-time implementation. I wrote the pulse-compression and Doppler-processing kernels in C++ for the receiver’s processing board — a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ SoC — under a hard per-pulse timing constraint of 10 microseconds. The board’s limited on-chip memory required a streaming architecture that processed each range line in place before the next pulse arrived. Getting the FFT pipeline within budget while keeping numerical precision at low SNR meant several rounds of fixed-point scaling and cache-aware profiling against captured field data.

My training supports this directly. My MSc at Rheinmark TU Aachen was in Electrical Engineering, and my thesis on adaptive spatial filtering for narrowband interference suppression in array receivers gave me a grounding in the mathematics of array processing and spatial filtering that I have drawn on throughout my career. The programme’s emphasis on linear algebra and transform theory has proved equally lasting, and the balance of electromagnetic theory and statistical signal processing mapped closely onto the work I have done since.

Kaikuvaara’s scope — SAR payloads, scatterometer electronics, ground-segment processing — sits well within my experience at Nordkom, and the chance to bring nearly two decades of that experience into a team with a different platform heritage and customer base is something I would genuinely value. I would be happy to discuss how my background matches your current requirements.

Yours sincerely,
Camille Rossi
